title: The Compilation Process
learning_outcomes: Explain the purpose of the compilation process in a C#/.NET program.
Predict the result of the included C# example and verify the documented output.
Apply the compilation process to a small task and identify one relevant boundary, limitation, or version requirement.

content.intro: The Compilation Process is lesson 17 in C# Program Structure and Syntax. Program structure is the set of rules that makes source code parseable and executable: statements, names, namespaces, entry points, and compiler/build stages. When a diagnostic appears, use its file and line context to isolate the smallest invalid construct.
content.why_it_matters: Clear program structure makes code easier to compile, review, debug, and maintain. This lesson focuses on the compilation process and shows how to verify the behavior instead of relying on assumptions.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: Program structure is the set of rules that makes source code parseable and executable: statements, names, namespaces, entry points, and compiler/build stages. When a diagnostic appears, use its file and line context to isolate the smallest invalid construct.

content_blocks.title: A practical way to learn it
content_blocks.text: Start with the smallest valid case for the compilation process. Predict the output, run or inspect the example in the stated toolchain, then change one input or rule and compare the result. For production code, record assumptions and verify boundary cases.

items.title: Source code and compilation
items.text: Separate source diagnostics, emitted assembly artifacts, and runtime execution; they are different stages with different failure modes.

items.title: Compiler diagnostics
items.text: Separate source diagnostics, emitted assembly artifacts, and runtime execution; they are different stages with different failure modes.

items.title: Assemblies and executable output
items.text: For assemblies and executable output, define the expected behavior, inspect how it relates to the compilation process, and verify a representative case plus one boundary or failure case.

items.title: Build configurations
items.text: Keep environment-specific configuration outside source code. Read settings at a clear boundary, validate required values on startup, and never commit credentials or print them in diagnostics.

items.title: Debug and Release builds
items.text: Create a reproducible case, inspect the state at the failure boundary, and log structured context that helps diagnosis.

items.title: Compilation errors vs runtime errors
items.text: Separate source diagnostics, emitted assembly artifacts, and runtime execution; they are different stages with different failure modes.

content.task: Try it yourself: create a small C# example that demonstrates the compilation process. Change one input or implementation detail, predict the result, then check it locally and explain one edge case.
task_acceptance_criteria: The example demonstrates the compilation process rather than only repeating its definition.
The result is checked locally or against a clearly documented reference output.
At least one relevant boundary, invalid-input case, or compatibility condition is considered.
hints: List the assumptions and expected behavior for the compilation process before editing the code.
Change one variable or rule at a time; keep the previous output for comparison.
If behavior differs, confirm the compiler/target framework and consult the linked official documentation.
content.solution_notes: Suggested approach: identify the expected input and output, start from the smallest example, use the feature only where it clarifies the rule, and verify both a typical case and a boundary/failure case.

common_mistakes.problem: Assuming the feature works identically on every target
common_mistakes.why: Language syntax, libraries, and runtime support are version-dependent.
common_mistakes.fix: Check the target framework and official versioned reference before using the feature.

common_mistakes.why: Boundary values, malformed input, and failure states often expose the real bug.
common_mistakes.fix: Add one typical input and one boundary or invalid case to the manual or automated checks.

common_mistakes.problem: Treating sample output as proof that the code ran
common_mistakes.why: The course reader uses static reference output for C# because it has no C# execution runner.
common_mistakes.fix: Run the snippet in a local .NET project or a separately isolated execution service.
